welcome.title: Welcome to DropFlow
welcome.drag.mac: Drag a file in Finder and, while still holding the mouse button, tap ⇧ Shift to convert, ⌘ Command for tools or ⌃ Control for actions. Drop the file on a slice of the wheel.
welcome.drag.linux: Drag a file and, while still holding the mouse button, tap Shift to convert, Ctrl for tools or Alt for actions. Drop the file on a slice of the wheel.
welcome.gnome.signout: On GNOME, DropFlow uses its small Shell extension to see the keys during a drag. It is installed: sign out and back in once to turn it on.
welcome.gnome.error: The DropFlow Shell extension could not be turned on. Open the Extensions app and turn on “DropFlow drag helper”.
welcome.click: On this desktop no app can watch drags. Right-click files in your file manager and choose “Open with DropFlow” to get the same wheel.
welcome.clickAlso: You can also right-click files in your file manager and choose “Open with DropFlow”.
welcome.mac.gatekeeper: DropFlow is free and is not notarized by Apple. If macOS blocks it, right-click the app and choose Open, or go to System Settings → Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway. You only need to do this once.
welcome.mac.menubar: DropFlow lives in the menu bar, at the top right of the screen.
welcome.linux.tray: DropFlow lives in the system tray. On GNOME the tray icon needs the “AppIndicator and KStatusNotifierItem” extension.
welcome.privacy: Everything happens on this computer. Nothing is uploaded.
settings.output.hint: Originals are never changed or replaced.
settings.login: Start DropFlow when I sign in

settings.engines.unixHint: DropFlow never installs programs by itself. To add one, copy its command and run it in a terminal.
